# Measured Split q\* = m·B_P/B_H in Sovereign Swarm / Flock Consensus

## 1. Context and Model

In a sovereign swarm, N autonomous nodes coordinate without central authority. Work arrives as a stream of tasks (transactions, proofs, state transitions). Each node routes work along two independent resource paths:

- **Path P** (peer-to-peer): direct horizontal routing between sovereign peers.
- **Path H** (hub): vertical routing through relay/aggregation infrastructure.

Both paths must drain their assigned queues simultaneously so no node idles waiting on the other at the commit barrier. The split ratio q\* governs how incoming work is partitioned.

---

## 2. Precise Definition

### 2.1 Quantities

| Symbol | Meaning | Units |
|--------|---------|-------|
| \(C_i\) | Raw link capacity of path \(i \in \{P,H\}\) | bytes/s |
| \(o_i\) | Protocol overhead fraction (headers, ACKs, retransmits) | dimensionless \([0,1)\) |
| \(B_i\) | Effective bandwidth: \(B_i = C_i(1 - o_i)\) | bytes/s |
| \(\varepsilon_i\) | Measured efficiency: fraction of \(B_i\) actually realized under load | dimensionless \((0,1]\) |
| \(E_i\) | End-to-end realized throughput: \(E_i = B_i \cdot \varepsilon_i\) | bytes/s |
| \(m\) | Efficiency ratio: \(m = \varepsilon_P / \varepsilon_H\) | dimensionless |
| \(W\) | Total workload to partition | bytes |
| \(q^\*\) | Optimal split ratio (work to P : work to H) | dimensionless |

### 2.2 Definition of q\*

> **Definition.** The measured split \(q^\*\) is the unique positive real number satisfying
>
> $$q^* = \frac{E_P}{E_H} = \frac{B_P \,\varepsilon_P}{B_H \,\varepsilon_H} = m \cdot \frac{B_P}{B_H}$$
>
> such that when a workload \(W\) is partitioned into \(W_P = \dfrac{q^\*\,W}{1+q^\*}\) and \(W_H = \dfrac{W}{1+q^\*}\), both paths complete in identical wall-clock time:
>
> $$T_P = \frac{W_P}{E_P} = \frac{W_H}{E_H} = T_H$$

### 2.3 Why the form \(m \cdot B_P/B_H\)

Raw bandwidth alone does not guarantee simultaneous finish because realized throughput degrades differently per path under concurrent load, encryption cost, queueing, and topology-dependent jitter. The factor \(m\) absorbs all such systematic asymmetry into a single scalar. Without \(m\) (i.e., \(m=1\)), the split reduces to the naive bandwidth-proportional rule, which is correct only when both paths have identical efficiency profiles.

---

## 3. Schema

```protobuf
message PathMetrics {
  string path_id          = 1;  // "P" or "H"
  double raw_capacity     = 2;  // bytes/s, link-layer measured
  double overhead_frac    = 3;  // [0,1), protocol tax
  double eff_bandwidth    = 4;  // computed: raw_capacity * (1 - overhead_frac)
  double efficiency       = 5;  // (0,1], measured under load
  double rtt_ms           = 6;  // round-trip time
  uint64 samples_taken    = 7;
  uint64 last_updated_ns  = 8;  // monotonic clock
}

message SplitState {
  PathMetrics path_p      = 1;
  PathMetrics path_h      = 2;
  double m                = 3;  // eps_P / eps_H
  double q_star           = 4;  // m * Bp / Bh
  double ci_lower         = 5;  // 95% CI lower bound on q_star
  double ci_upper         = 6;  // 95% CI upper bound
  uint64 epoch            = 7;  // consensus epoch at which q_star was agreed
  uint32 quorum_size      = 8;  // number of nodes contributing measurements
}

message WorkAssignment {
  uint64 total_workload   = 1;  // bytes
  uint64 work_to_path_p   = 2;  // floor(total * q_star / (1 + q_star))
  uint64 work_to_path_h   = 3;  // remainder
}
```

---

## 4. Exact Algorithm

### Phase 0 — Initialization

Every node starts with priors: \(\varepsilon_P^{(0)} = \varepsilon_H^{(0)} = 1.0\), hence \(q^{*(0)} = B_P/B_H\).

---

### Phase 1 — Bandwidth Measurement

Each node probes both paths with \(K\) bulk transfers of size \(S\) bytes.

```
for k = 1 to K:
    t_start ← monotonic_clock()
    send S bytes over path i
    await full ACK
    t_end ← monotonic_clock()
    record throughput_k = S / (t_end − t_start)

B_i ← median({throughput_1, …, throughput_K})
```

Set \(K = 16\), \(S = 1\,\text{MiB}\). Use median for robustness against outliers.

---

### Phase 2 — Efficiency Measurement

Efficiency \(\varepsilon_i\) is measured by comparing achieved throughput under realistic concurrent load vs. isolated bulk transfer.

```
for trial t = 1 to T:
    launch background traffic at 80% of B_i (simulating production load)
    concurrently, send probe of size S_probe over path i
    record achieved_throughput_t

ε_i ← mean({achieved_throughput_t}) / B_i
```

Set \(T = 32\), \(S_{\text{probe}} = 256\,\text{KiB}\).

---

### Phase 3 — Compute m and q\*

```
m     ← ε_P / ε_H
q_star ← m × (B_P / B_H)
```

Compute confidence interval via bootstrap over the \(T\) efficiency samples:

```
for b = 1 to 1000:
    resample ε_P*, ε_H* from measured distributions
    m_b     ← ε_P*_b / ε_H*_b
    q_b     ← m_b × (B_P / B_H)
sort {q_b}; take 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles as [ci_lower, ci_upper]
```

---

### Phase 4 — Flock Consensus on q\*

Since no node is sovereign over others, all nodes must agree on a single \(q^\*\) value. Use weighted median voting:

```
each node broadcasts (q_star_local, weight = 1 / variance_of_measurements)

collect all (q_star_j, weight_j) pairs from quorum_size ≥ ⌈2N/3⌉ + 1 nodes

q_star_global ← weighted_median({q_star_j}, weights = {weight_j})
```

All nodes set their local \(q^\*\) to \(q^\*_{\text{global}}\). This is deterministic given the same multiset of votes.

---

### Phase 5 — Apply Split

Given total workload \(W\) arriving at epoch boundary:

```
work_to_P ← floor(W × q_star / (1 + q_star))
work_to_H ← W − work_to_P
```

Enqueue `work_to_P` items onto path P queue, `work_to_H` onto path H queue.

---

### Phase 6 — Verify Convergence

At the next commit barrier:

```
t_finish_P ← timestamp when path P queue empties
t_finish_H ← timestamp when path H queue empties

drift ← |t_finish_P − t_finish_H| / min(t_finish_P, t_finish_H)

if drift ≤ τ:        // τ = 0.02 (2% tolerance)
    status ← CONVERGED
else:
    status ← DIVERGED
    trigger Phase 7
```

---

### Phase 7 — Adaptive Correction

If diverged, update efficiencies using observed completion times:

```
realized_E_P ← work_to_P / t_finish_P
realized_E_H ← work_to_H / t_finish_H

ε_P_new ← 0.7 × ε_P_old + 0.3 × (realized_E_P / B_P)
ε_H_new ← 0.7 × ε_H_old + 0.3 × (realized_E_H / B_H)

recompute m, q_star; go to Phase 4
```

The EWMA (exponentially weighted moving average) with decay 0.7 ensures stability while allowing adaptation to changing network conditions.

---

## 5. Correctness Argument

**Claim.** Under the split \(q^\* = m \cdot B_P/B_H\), both paths finish simultaneously.

**Proof.** Assign \(W_P = \frac{q^\* W}{1+q^\*}\) and \(W_H = \frac{W}{1+q^\*}\).

$$T_P = \frac{W_P}{E_P} = \frac{q^\* W}{(1+q^\*)\,E_P}, \qquad T_H = \frac{W_H}{E_H} = \frac{W}{(1+q^\*)\,E_H}$$

$$\frac{T_P}{T_H} = \frac{q^\*\,E_H}{E_P} = \frac{\left(m\,\frac{B_P}{B_H}\right)(B_H\,\varepsilon_H)}{B_P\,\varepsilon_P} = \frac{m\,B_P\,\varepsilon_H}{B_P\,\varepsilon_P} = \frac{\varepsilon_P\,\varepsilon_H}{\varepsilon_H\,\varepsilon_P} = 1 \quad \blacksquare$$

---

## 6. Edge Cases and Guards

| Condition | Guard |
|-----------|-------|
| \(B_H \to 0\) | Clamp \(q^\* \le q_{\max} = 1000\); overflow to P only |
| \(\varepsilon_i < 0.01\) | Mark path degraded; reroute all work to healthy path |
| Quorum not reached | Fall back to last agreed \(q^\*\); flag stale |
| Measurement variance too high (CV > 0.3) | Increase K and T; do not update \(q^\*\) until stable |
| Byzantine outlier vote | Trim top and bottom 10% of votes before weighted median |

---

## 7. Summary Formula Chain

$$\boxed{B_i = C_i(1-o_i) \;\to\; \varepsilon_i = \frac{\text{realized}}{B_i} \;\to\; m = \frac{\varepsilon_P}{\varepsilon_H} \;\to\; q^\* = m\cdot\frac{B_P}{B_H} \;\to\; W_P = \frac{q^\* W}{1+q^\*}}$$

This chain is deterministic, measurable, and converges under the adaptive loop because the EWMA update is a contraction mapping on \(\varepsilon\) with fixed point equal to true efficiency.
